name: Serengeti National Park
summary: Open plains, rocky outcrops and a remarkable movement of wildebeest make the Serengeti a landscape to explore slowly, not just a place to tick off.
planningNote: The instant planner covers central Serengeti. Migration locations and river crossings are never guaranteed; other sectors need a tailored route.

name: Ngorongoro Conservation Area
summary: A volcanic crater, highland scenery and an exceptional human-history record come together in this UNESCO-listed conservation landscape.
planningNote: Crater descent, vehicle charges and special-access activities need separate confirmation before a quote is final.

name: Tarangire National Park
summary: Elephants, baobabs and the Tarangire River give this northern park a character of its own, with changing wildlife concentrations across the seasons.
planningNote: Allow time for game drives away from the entrance. Wildlife movements depend on water and rainfall.

name: Lake Manyara National Park
summary: A Rift Valley lake and its surrounding woodland create a compact change of scenery on a northern safari, particularly for travellers interested in birds.
planningNote: Lake levels and bird concentrations change. Confirm the current status of optional activities separately.

name: Arusha National Park
summary: Mount Meru, the Momella lakes and a mix of forest and open country offer a different perspective on the northern safari landscape.
planningNote: Ask an advisor to arrange this extension. Guided walks and any canoe activity require separate arrangements.

name: Kilimanjaro National Park
summary: Africa's highest mountain rises through distinct landscapes towards Kibo, Mawenzi and the Shira plateau. A climb deserves its own carefully planned expedition.
planningNote: Climbs are advisor-assisted. Route, acclimatisation time, qualified guides, equipment and appropriate insurance must be reviewed; a summit is not guaranteed.

name: Mkomazi National Park
summary: Mkomazi adds a conservation-focused stop to northern Tanzania, with a protected landscape associated with black rhino and African wild dog programmes.
planningNote: Sanctuary visits are not the same as a general game drive. Confirm access, reservations and additional charges with an advisor.

name: Nyerere National Park
summary: Woodlands, floodplains and river habitats support a varied southern safari, with the possibility of combining land-based wildlife viewing and permitted boat excursions.
planningNote: Boat and walking activities depend on the camp, operator, conditions and permissions; they are not automatically included in a draft.

name: Ruaha National Park
summary: Baobab-studded country and the Great Ruaha River frame a safari centred on wide landscapes, predators, elephants and patient wildlife watching.
planningNote: Allow realistic transfer time on a southern circuit. Confirm seasonal camp operations and road or air connections before booking.

name: Mikumi National Park
summary: The Mkata floodplain opens into broad grassland, with hippo pools and woodland adding variety to game drives on Tanzania's southern circuit.
planningNote: Match transfer days to your arrival and departure plans. Optional activities require operator confirmation.

name: Udzungwa Mountains National Park
summary: Rainforest trails, Sanje's cascading water and range-restricted primates make Udzungwa a walking-focused contrast to the open savanna.
planningNote: An advisor should match the guided trail to your fitness and the weather. Do not assume a waterfall route is suitable for everyone.

name: Kitulo National Park
summary: Highland grasslands, wildflowers and birds give Kitulo a botanical focus, with open walking country quite unlike a classic big-game safari.
planningNote: Flowering follows seasonal conditions. Request a guided highland itinerary and prepare for variable weather.

name: Katavi National Park
summary: The Katuma River and seasonal floodplains shape a remote safari landscape known for hippos, crocodiles and large gatherings of buffalo.
planningNote: Plan with an advisor: flights, road access, camp openings and supplies need coordination in this remote part of the country.

name: Mahale Mountains National Park
summary: Forested mountains meet Lake Tanganyika at Mahale, where guided chimpanzee trekking is the centrepiece of a forest-and-lake journey.
planningNote: Trekking permits, age and health rules, fitness, boat transfers and camp availability need confirmation. Chimpanzee sightings remain wildlife encounters, not promises.

name: Gombe National Park
summary: Gombe's forested lakeshore is closely associated with chimpanzee research and offers a specialised primate-focused addition to a western Tanzania journey.
planningNote: Arrange authorised guides and transfers. Confirm current age, health and viewing rules before committing to a trek.

name: Rubondo Island National Park
summary: Forest, papyrus margins and quiet coves create an island safari on Lake Victoria, with birdlife and conservation stories at its heart.
planningNote: Confirm boat or air access and available guided activities. Primate programmes should not be assumed to guarantee sightings.

name: Saanane Island National Park
summary: Granite rocks, footpaths and lake viewpoints make this island park a nature-focused outing from Mwanza on Lake Victoria.
planningNote: Ask an advisor to confirm the boat transfer, guided visit and current visitor arrangements.

name: Burigi-Chato National Park
summary: Lakes and savanna provide the setting for a less familiar wildlife journey in northwestern Tanzania.
planningNote: This is a tailored extension. Confirm the operating gate, guiding, accommodation and road conditions before travel.

name: Ibanda-Kyerwa National Park
summary: This Kagera park brings a northwestern wildlife stop into a journey through Tanzania's borderland landscapes.
planningNote: Advisor-assisted only: confirm access, ranger services, visitor facilities and overnight arrangements before including it in a route.

name: Rumanyika-Karagwe National Park
summary: Explore a lesser-known protected landscape in Kagera as part of a carefully arranged northwestern Tanzania itinerary.
planningNote: Ask an advisor to verify current access and guiding. This catalogue listing is not confirmation of available tourism services.

name: Ugalla River National Park
summary: Miombo woodland and seasonally flooded grassland surround the Ugalla River, creating a remote landscape for specialist wildlife journeys.
planningNote: An advisor must check seasonal access, permitted activities, guiding and camp logistics before proposing a visit.

name: Kigosi landscape
summary: Kigosi appears in TANAPA's park directory as a western wilderness destination, but published official listings are not fully consistent.
planningNote: Current management, tourism access and permitted activities must be verified directly before any itinerary or booking is offered.

name: Saadani National Park
summary: Coastal grasslands, mangroves and the Wami estuary bring safari landscapes close to the Indian Ocean.
planningNote: Game drives, river trips and beach access need a coordinated plan. Follow ranger advice around waterways and wildlife.

name: Olduvai Gorge
summary: Olduvai's fossil and stone-tool record adds a human-history perspective to the Ngorongoro and Serengeti landscapes.
planningNote: Ask an advisor to include the visitor experience and applicable conservation-area access. Excavation areas are not freely accessible.

name: Stone Town of Zanzibar
summary: A UNESCO-listed Swahili trading town where narrow streets and historic buildings record centuries of Indian Ocean exchange.
planningNote: A local guided walk adds context. Confirm individual monument openings and respect worship, residents and photography preferences.

name: Kilwa Kisiwani & Songo Mnara
summary: The remains of these island trading settlements reveal the architecture and maritime connections of the medieval Swahili coast.
planningNote: Arrange local guides, permissions and suitable boats; tides and sea conditions affect visits. Never climb fragile structures.

name: Kondoa Rock-Art Sites
summary: Painted rock shelters preserve a remarkable cultural record within the landscapes around Kondoa, recognised on UNESCO's World Heritage List.
planningNote: Visit with an authorised local guide. Respect living cultural practices and do not touch or wet the paintings.

name: Bagamoyo & Kaole
summary: Bagamoyo's coastal buildings, museums and nearby Kaole ruins offer a thoughtful encounter with Swahili history and the region's caravan and slave-trade past.
planningNote: Book a locally guided heritage visit and confirm opening arrangements. Allow time for context, not just photographs.

name: Zanzibar Island / Unguja
summary: Combine an Indian Ocean stay with Swahili heritage, spice-growing traditions and island nature on Unguja, the main island commonly called Zanzibar.
planningNote: An advisor will match the coast to your interests and tides, and confirm transfers, activities and current entry requirements.

name: Pemba Island
summary: Pemba combines green island scenery, coastal communities and a quieter setting for a separately planned Zanzibar archipelago escape.
planningNote: Confirm inter-island transport and accommodation before travel. Marine excursions need a qualified operator and suitable conditions.

name: Jozani-Chwaka Bay
summary: A forest-focused change of pace on Unguja, with Zanzibar red colobus among the species visitors hope to observe on guided walks.
planningNote: Use authorised guides, keep your distance from wildlife and avoid feeding or touching monkeys. Sightings cannot be guaranteed.

name: Nungwi & Kendwa
summary: Northern Unguja offers beach time alongside the maritime character of Nungwi and the neighbouring coast around Kendwa.
planningNote: Choose a beach base with an advisor. Confirm swimming conditions, transfers and the operator of any boat activity.

name: Mnemba marine area
summary: The waters around Mnemba are associated with reef excursions and marine exploration off Zanzibar.
planningNote: The island is private; a marine excursion does not grant island access. Confirm permissions, sea conditions and responsible reef practices.

name: Chumbe Island
summary: Chumbe brings coral-reef conservation and island forest together in a small-scale nature experience near Zanzibar.
planningNote: Visits require advance confirmation with the operator; do not assume daily access or available accommodation.

name: Mafia Island & Marine Park
summary: Coral reefs, seagrass and mangroves make Mafia a destination for travellers interested in marine habitats as well as island time.
planningNote: Confirm the location of your stay, marine-park permissions and charges, transfers and dive or snorkel arrangements separately.

name: Mnazi Bay-Ruvuma Estuary Marine Park
summary: Near Tanzania's southern coast, protected reefs, mangroves and seagrass offer a marine-focused extension around Mtwara.
planningNote: Ask an advisor to confirm permitted excursions, local operators, accommodation and suitable sea conditions.

name: Pangani
summary: A river mouth and historic coastal town offer a slower mainland-coast stop, with opportunities to explore local heritage and river scenery.
planningNote: Confirm your coastal base and transfers with an advisor. River and ocean activities require separate operator arrangements.

name: Maziwe Marine Reserve
summary: Off the Pangani coast, Maziwe provides a marine-reserve excursion that can complement time on the mainland shore.
planningNote: Boat departures and access depend on tides, weather and permissions. Arrange a licensed operator and appropriate safety equipment.

name: Bongoyo & Mbudya Islands
summary: These protected islands off Dar es Salaam bring an offshore nature break within reach of a city-based itinerary.
planningNote: Confirm the landing point, authorised boat, reserve fees and weather. No boat departure or swimming condition is guaranteed.

name: Amboni Caves
summary: Limestone passages near Tanga add a geological and cultural stop to a journey along the northern mainland coast.
planningNote: Visit with an authorised guide. Discuss confined spaces, footing and accessibility before choosing a cave route.

name: Usambara Mountains
summary: Forest, cultivated slopes and expansive viewpoints make the Usambaras a walking destination, with Lushoto a gateway to the western range.
planningNote: Arrange locally guided walks suited to your fitness. Routes can be muddy, and community visits should be agreed with hosts.

name: Amani / East Usambara forests
summary: The wetter eastern Usambaras offer forest biodiversity and a nature-focused counterpart to the viewpoints and villages around Lushoto.
planningNote: Confirm reserve access, a specialist guide and local accommodation. Bird and wildlife sightings are not assured.

name: Lake Natron
summary: An alkaline Rift Valley lake beneath volcanic country, Natron is an important flamingo habitat and a striking landscape in its own right.
planningNote: Use local guides, avoid sensitive breeding areas and plan for heat and remote access. This is not a swimming-lake recommendation.

name: Lake Eyasi
summary: A seasonal Rift Valley lake south of the Serengeti highlands, with changing water levels and opportunities for birding and respectful community-led visits.
planningNote: Visits with Hadza or Datoga hosts must be arranged with consent and fair local benefit. Ask before photographing anyone.

name: Lake Chala
summary: A crater lake on the Tanzania-Kenya border offers dramatic rim scenery and birding interests east of Kilimanjaro.
planningNote: Arrange access on the Tanzanian side and a suitable guided route. Confirm activity safety locally; swimming is not assumed to be suitable.

name: Lake Tanganyika
summary: Tanzania's western lakeshore links fishing communities, forested mountain backdrops and gateway towns such as Kigoma and Ujiji.
planningNote: Distances are substantial. Confirm boats, flight or road connections and local water safety before planning activities.

name: Lake Victoria
summary: Islands, fishing livelihoods and broad water horizons give Tanzania's Lake Victoria shore its own travel rhythm beyond the safari parks.
planningNote: Choose a specific lakeshore base with an advisor. Check current transport and water-safety advice rather than assuming boat or swimming access.

name: Lake Nyasa & Matema
summary: At Matema, the mountains meet Lake Nyasa in a lakeshore setting that can complement a southern-highlands journey.
planningNote: Confirm overland connections and your chosen accommodation. Seek current local safety and health advice before entering freshwater.

name: Lake Ngozi
summary: A forested crater in the Uporoto highlands near Mbeya rewards a guided walk with views down towards the lake.
planningNote: Use a local guide and suitable footwear. Confirm trail conditions; steep terrain and weather can change the difficulty.

name: Kalambo Falls
summary: The Kalambo River drops into a dramatic gorge on the Tanzania-Zambia border, adding a waterfall landscape to a Lake Tanganyika journey.
planningNote: Arrange the Tanzanian approach with a guide and verify road conditions. Water flow is seasonal; keep well back from unprotected edges.

name: Mbozi Meteorite
summary: A large iron meteorite in Songwe offers a distinctive natural-history stop on a journey through Tanzania's southwestern highlands.
planningNote: Ask an advisor to confirm site access and a guided stop. Treat the protected monument with care.

name: Mount Meru
summary: Mount Meru anchors Arusha National Park and adds a mountain-focused objective to a northern Tanzania journey.
planningNote: A summit trek needs its own guided plan, permits, equipment and time for altitude. It is not included in a standard park day visit.

name: Ol Doinyo Lengai
summary: This active volcano rises near Lake Natron and forms a powerful focal point in northern Tanzania's Rift Valley landscape.
planningNote: Do not assume climbing is open or appropriate. Current volcanic conditions, permissions, specialist guidance and fitness must be reviewed first.

name: Isimila Stone Age Site
summary: Near Iringa, Isimila combines a Stone Age archaeological story with an eroded landscape of pillars and gullies.
planningNote: Arrange a guided visit and allow for uneven ground. Leave artefacts and natural formations undisturbed.
